extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance in education (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel implementing Title IX pregnancy/lactation provisions
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX pregnancy and lactation compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for education recipients on implementing final §106.40(b)(3)–(b)(4) requirements: ensuring access to lactation space, limits on requiring supporting documentation for pregnancy-related modifications, and treating pregnancy-related conditions comparably to other temporary medical conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure student access to a lactation space (§106.40(b)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure that a student can access a lactation space that “may be used” for pumping or breastfeeding as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient's provision must be prompt and effective to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access; whether a particular space meets the standard is case-by-case but generally means the space is functional, appropriate, and safe. The requirement focuses on ensuring student access (not just availability). The Department declined to adopt additional size or setup requirements to preserve recipient flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility vs. Title IX Coordinator role
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is ultimately responsible for ensuring a student's access to a lactation space; the Title IX Coordinator must coordinate actions under §106.40(b)(3)(i)–(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.40(b)(3) to clarify that the recipient must take actions and the Title IX Coordinator coordinates them; see discussion of the Title IX Coordinator role for further explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to construct new lactation spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to construct new lactation spaces if an existing space otherwise meets the requirements of §106.40(b)(3)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department anticipates recipients will be able to comply using existing space at minimal cost; there is no requirement for a particular size, shape, or structural features. Recipients may allow students to access existing employee lactation spaces or other spaces that meet the requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion on location, number, and administration of lactation spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion in where a lactation space is located, the number of lactation spaces, and how they handle administration (including multi-user management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as the lactation space complies with §106.40(b)(3)(v), recipients may use signage, scheduling systems, or multi-person spaces separated by partitions; whether evening or weekend access is required depends on whether lack of access would frustrate a student's participation in education programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility regardless of gender identity or expression
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must ensure that any student who is lactating can voluntarily access a lactation space regardless of the student's gender identity or gender expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasized that recipients must provide access without regard to gender identity/expression and may use any preferred terminology in communications with students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on requiring supporting documentation except when necessary and reasonable (§106.40(b)(3)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not require supporting documentation for requests under §106.40(b)(3)(ii)–(v) unless the documentation is necessary and reasonable under the circumstances to determine the reasonable modifications or actions to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary and reasonable documentation generally includes no more than is sufficient to confirm—in a fair manner—that a student has a need related to pregnancy or related conditions that requires a modification. The Department added §106.40(b)(3)(vi) to clarify limits on documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exhaustive situations when documentation is not necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulation lists situations in which it would not be necessary and reasonable to require documentation and therefore a recipient may not require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list includes: (1) when the student's need for a specific action is obvious (e.g., asking for a different size uniform); (2) when the student has previously provided sufficient supporting documentation; (3) when the requested modification is one of four commonly sought modifications (carrying/keeping water nearby and drinking; using a bigger desk; sitting or standing; taking breaks to eat/drink/use restroom); (4) when the need concerns lactation/pumping; and (5) when the specific action is available to students for reasons other than pregnancy without submitting documentation. These situations are non-exhaustive and may overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples when documentation may be necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation may be necessary and reasonable when needed to determine a specific modification (e.g., healthcare provider documentation supporting medically ordered bed rest to justify access to online or homebound education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when documentation is reasonable, it must be limited to what is necessary to determine the modification; recipients should not ask for unrelated medical details (e.g., date of last menstrual cycle) and should avoid re-requesting documentation already provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student self-confirmation sufficient for lactation needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Student confirmation—or a simple request to access a recipient's lactation space—is sufficient confirmation of lactation or pumping needs; recipients must not require supporting documentation for lactation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes it is uncommon to obtain medical documentation regarding initiation of lactation and healthcare providers may be unable to document pumping or types of needed modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may not deny modifications based on improper documentation requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may not justify denial of a reasonable modification under §106.40(b)(3)(ii)–(v) based on lack of documentation if its request for documentation does not comport with §106.40(b)(3)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for documentation must comport with the necessity-and-reasonableness standard; otherwise denial on that basis is barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat pregnancy or related conditions comparably to other temporary medical conditions (§106.40(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent consistent with paragraph (b)(3), a recipient must treat pregnancy or related conditions in the same manner and under the same policies as any other temporary medical condition with respect to any medical or hospital benefit, service, plan, or policy the recipient administers, operates, offers, or participates in for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised proposed text to use “medical condition” (not “physical condition” or “temporary disability”) to avoid implying pregnancy is a disability; the provision applies regardless of whether pregnancy-related conditions qualify as disabilities under Section 504 or the ADA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-preemption of state or local lactation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not preempt State or local laws that require lactation spaces to have certain features (e.g., chair, flat surface, electrical outlet, running water, refrigerated storage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may offer additional features in lactation spaces as reasonable modifications; the Department may consider commenters' suggestions in technical assistance but did not adopt mandatory federal feature requirements in this rule.
